content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: both queues are predicted at 100% service level for 15:30-17:30, against an 80% target.","why":"Both queues are running below planned headcount. Payments had 31 and 34 agents against 37 and 42 planned, and general had 31 and 34 against 38 and 41. Even so, volume is close to forecast and handle time is below forecast. The model predicts 100% service level on both queues with 0% abandons through 17:30, and 97.8% for the rest of the day, at no extra cost. The feeds don't explain the staffing gap, since absence is normal and there is no incident or campaign. It is worth checking for unscheduled meetings, training or late returns from breaks.","trade_offs":["P1 (IVR callbacks on both queues 18:00-20:00) costs nothing and predicts the same results as no action (100% now, 97.8% rest of day). It is a safety net you could add if the evening worsens.","P2 also moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 18:00-19:00. It costs nothing but lowers the rest-of-day figure to 97.3%, so it takes cover away from general without any gain.","P3 deflects 20% of new-offer enquiries on general to chat and adds a payments callback. It costs ₹60 and inconveniences customers, and the window is still 100%, with the rest of the day slightly lower at 97.7%."],"watch":"Watch whether actual headcount keeps falling short of plan, especially on general where volume is +6.2%, and follow up on the unexplained gap. If the gap widens toward 18:00, consider switching on the no-cost evening callbacks (P1). No escalation is flagged."}
